newsitem.title: EGYPT: Hebron deal close, Christopher says.
newsitem.headline: Hebron deal close, Christopher says.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Tuesday he thought Israel and the Palestinians were close to a deal on Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.

"The current negotiations have been intensive and at times frustrating. But I believe that a final set of very specific understandings on Hebron is close at hand," he told the opening session of a Middle East economic conference in Cairo.

Christopher met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Cairo on Monday night during a last flurry of diplomatic activity before the conference opened. But U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns reported "no discernible progress".
All parties have tried to discourage persistent rumours that a Hebron deal might be signed during the Cairo conference.
Christopher said that once the Hebron negotiations succeeded, "I urge the parties to move ahead with the same urgency to implement the remainder of the Interim Agreement."
"For these and future negotiations to succeed, each side must go the extra mile to understand the needs of the other -- to take their requirements into account," he added.
"Each side must recognise that it is not possible to make peace without taking risks -- but that maintaining the status quo poses even greater risks for the future," he said.
